title: Skyrmion Phase Control by Magnetic Dipole-Dipole Interaction and Electric Field in Centrosymmetric Materials
authors: Raz Rivlis, Alexander Petrović, Yuri Dahnovsky
abstract: Establishing precise control over the helicity and spatial configuration of magnetic skyrmions will be essential to realize their promise in classical, analog and quantum computation applications. In this work, we explore the role of magnetic dipole-dipole interactions, external electric fields, and magnetic fields in controlling these parameters within a triangular lattice centrosymmetric skyrmion host. We demonstrate that dipole-dipole interactions strongly favor Bloch helicity. Notably, a zero magnetic field skyrmion phase appears upon raising the dipole-dipole coupling strength, with substantial potential for cost-effective quantum device applications. We also report the emergence of a meron/antimeron lattice phase, in the absence of any Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. In contrast, applied electric fields stabilize high density Néel skyrmion crystals. The interplay between dipole-dipole interactions and external electric fields creates a continuous transition between the two skyrmion types, rather than an abrupt switch. Applied electric fields can therefore be used as a continuous tuning mechanism for skyrmion helicity, and hence a control handle for tuning two-level systems in skyrmion qubits.
summary: The research explores controlling magnetic skyrmions in centrosymmetric lattices by manipulating dipole-dipole interactions and external electric fields. Key findings include the ability of electric fields to continuously tune the skyrmion helicity, providing a mechanism for tuning qubits. This work advances the understanding of topological spin control crucial for next-generation quantum devices.
main_problem: The primary goal is establishing precise control over the helicity and spatial configuration of magnetic skyrmions for use in advanced computational applications.
main_result: The study shows that electric fields can continuously tune the skyrmion helicity, offering a novel control handle for tuning two-level systems within skyrmion qubits. Furthermore, dipole-dipole interactions stabilize Bloch helicity and induce new lattice phases even at zero magnetic field.
method: Theoretical modeling using classical spin vector models solved via Monte Carlo simulations (Metropolis-Hastings algorithm) to map out phase diagrams.
model_or_system: The system is a skyrmion host on a triangular lattice, modeled by an extended Heisenberg Hamiltonian incorporating nearest-neighbor, next-nearest-neighbor, and third-nearest-neighbor exchange interactions. The model explicitly includes magnetic dipole-dipole interactions and external electric fields.
key_observables: Topological charge (Q), Root Mean Square of the topological charge ($	ext{QRMS}$), and the balance between skyrmion/antiskyrmion populations ($ ar{Q}/	ext{QRMS}$).
important_parameters: Dipole-dipole coupling strength ($C$), external electric field strength, magnetic field ($B_z$), and lattice exchange couplings ($J_2, J_3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is based on a classical spin vector model ($\mathbf{S}$), and phase boundaries are qualitatively defined due to strong thermal fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of magnetic phases (Ferromagnetic, Skyrmion Crystal, Helical) across parameter space ($J_2$ vs $J_3$) and show real-space spin textures corresponding to different helicity types (Bloch vs. Néel).
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates the influence of dipole-dipole interactions on skyrmion stability, demonstrating phase transitions at zero field. It then analyzes how applied electric fields mediate a continuous transition between Bloch and Néel skyrmion states.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental control mechanisms (electric fields) over topological spin textures, which is highly relevant to developing robust quantum memory elements based on magnetic materials.
